decisions.decision: The coined term signature skeleton is DROPPED. No invented vocabulary.
decisions.rationale: Owner instruction. The prior rationale was FALSE, not merely weak, and the document's own table falsified it: four owned sources name the artifact and multiple rows populate the cell described as unnamed. The replacement warrant is stronger -- no UNAMBIGUOUS name exists, because every available name reuses a word another owned source commits to a different cell. decisions.decision: Axis one is production-side versus TEST-side; three axes total (where it lives, what it stands in for, lifetime).

Three axes because all four combinations of the first two are populated by owned sources, and the fourth cell rescues a caveat that existed only as an exception because no cell held it.

decisions.decision: The vintage/seniority paragraph is replaced by an INDEPENDENCE claim -- no chronology, no lineage, no seniority in any form.

decisions.decision: Tier reliability is qualified three ways: claim type, source medium, source version.

context_notes: THE GUARDS WORKED, which is the most important result. The executor tripped its own gates three times and each was caught: a header comment added a fourth mention of the label constant and broke the ==3 assertion; its first section-5 draft reproduced the banned no-author phrasing VERBATIM and G2 caught its own author; and the RED-BASELINE table's row ids collided with the roster count. It also reported three verify commands as weak rather than treating their passes as evidence -- an anchor loop that succeeds on an empty list, two lower-bound assertions that catch a dropped guard but not an added one, and a grep with no exit-status wrapper -- and measured exact equality by hand instead. That is the discipline this whole revision existed to install. EIGHT of my own errors were caught this session, mostly by the owner or a subagent: I read source prose from four .oracle/ entry documents (firewall breach -- use ls and find for existence only); I briefed both acceptance reviewers with a two-dot diff across a merge boundary, which FABRICATED a finding in one report; three counts I asserted were contradicted by measurement (the checker's coinage reference, SKILL.md's absent guard, and the historical occurrence count where five was claimed and THREE measured); I announced dispatching a revision and did not send it; I recommended deleting the Usenet mbox having forgotten the conversion was selective; and I told the owner the owned oracle path was more accurate than web research when the opposite held on the table question. The pattern across all nine checker findings is one thing: controls that report success without verifying anything. Seven false-GREENs, and the plan's own author found an eighth in its own work.
